To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intrahepatic HCV-specific T cells are the most important cells for controlling HCV infection and that they expand very rapidly when HCV is present.

(a) the frequency of clonal HCV-specific T cells in liver is 10 times higher than in blood; (b) the peak clonal response is concurrent with peak viral load; (c) the clonal response in liver is maintained for at least three months after the clearance; and (d) the clonal T cell response rebounds before CD8+ T cell numbers are restored.

(1) HCV-specific T cells expand in the liver after viral challenge, (2) HCV-specific clonal expansion occurs prior to an increase in CD8+ T cell values, (3) the magnitude of clonal expansion is higher in the liver, and (4) HCV-specific expansion is maintained for at least three months after viral clearance.

the development of new methods for the detection of virus-specific T-cell clones in the blood and liver of chimpanzees.
